Tarpa Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tarpa, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews first settled in Tarpa in the mid-18th century, though the first census record dates to 1880 (195 Jews); population grew to 245 by 1930. The community maintained a cheder, burial society, mikveh, and synagogue, joining the Orthodox stream in 1876. In 1941, young men were conscripted for forced labor; following German occupation, residents were gathered in the synagogue and transferred to the Beregszász Ghetto before deportation to Auschwitz. Only 19 survivors returned, all of whom soon left. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1931, its newest to 1944.
